solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The very thing provided for fear that upset is involved

indicators.note: is involved means one piece is wrapped up inside the other

parts.note: provided, as in 'provided that', means if

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the word is turned over, read from the bottom

parts.note: lest is an old word meaning for fear that

explanation.surface: Someone describes an object whose very presence is guarded against out of fear of a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an emphatic pronoun, the word stresses that something is that very object and nothing else.

clue.text: Chamber group a great success? Time to move forward.

indicators.note: to move forward tells us the time letter shifts to the front of the word

parts.note: a riot is a big hit, a show that is a great success

explanation.surface: A reviewer asks whether a chamber ensemble was a hit, then says it is time to move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move forward' shifts the T of RIOT from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber group of three players, such as a piano trio, is the classic small ensemble.

clue.text: Experimental area absent from Tory speeches?

parts.note: a party that is not Tory, in British politics, is Labour, shortened to Lab
oratory is the art of making speeches, or speeches collectively

explanation.surface: A jibe that experiments are missing from Conservative party speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK politics the main rival of the Tories (Conservatives) is Labour, abbreviated LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a room or building set aside for scientific experiments.

clue.text: Dancing ingénue nugatory in American musical

indicators.note: dancing letters move around, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the accent
taken as written

explanation.surface: An inexperienced young actress dances worthlessly in a Broadway show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges INGENUE plus NUGATORY, fifteen letters, into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: This Irving Berlin show about the sharpshooter Annie Oakley is a famous Broadway musical.

clue.text: Not entirely cross — sensible, suppressing anger — it's not very heated

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a rood is a cross or crucifix, as in a church's rood screen

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something down within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: mature means sensible, grown-up in judgement
temper means anger, as in losing one's temper

explanation.surface: Advice to someone a bit cross: be sensible and hold down your anger, it isn't heated.
explanation.walkthrough: A rood is a church's cross, the old word behind the rood screen.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the ordinary ambient warmth of a room, so something at that level is neither chilled nor heated.

clue.text: Special label for men only

parts.note: a tag is a label tied or attached to something

explanation.surface: A special tag marks something reserved for men alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is an event restricted to male guests.

clue.text: Italian writer: "I governed valley covered by Italian river"

indicators.note: covered by means sitting inside the other piece, which wraps round it

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy
taken as written
ran means governed, as in ran the country
a dell is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: An Italian author quoted as saying he ruled a valley beneath a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Italian playwright of Six Characters in Search of an Author and a Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Car problem has cricketer out in flannel

indicators.note: out means removed, as a batsman who is out leaves the field

parts.note: a flat battery stops a car from starting
a bat is a batsman, a cricketer who bats

explanation.surface: A car breaks down while a cricketer in flannels is dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes BAT from FLAT BATTERY. Cricket whites were traditionally flannel trousers, the surface's false sense; here flannel is smooth, insincere talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang flannel is evasive or ingratiating talk, which is close kin to excessive praise.

clue.text: Aquatic bird accepting endless bad weather in country

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rain is the bad weather

explanation.surface: A seabird puts up with rain that never quite stops while out in open country.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain means a stretch of land with its physical features, the sense of country in 'rough country'.

clue.text: No coming back by criminal gang left for dead in court

indicators.note: coming back means read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: for here means in place of, swapping one letter in for another

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese criminal gang

explanation.surface: A criminal gang member can't return, abandoned for dead, and ends up in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns NO into ON; 'left for dead' swaps L for the D of TRIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A person being tried is in court facing the judge, which is the plain sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Coming to American ground after one takes flight? That could be me

definitions.text: Coming to American ground after one takes flight? That could be me

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are reworked
takes flight means leaves, so the letter for one is removed from the pool

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
one is A, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A migrant speaks: arriving on US soil after fleeing, that could be me.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the sixteen letters of COMING TO AMERICAN, remove A ('one takes flight') and rearrange ('ground') the rest. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moving to another country for better work and pay is exactly the person who arrives seeking a living.

clue.text: View on craze involving navy? Nonsense

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the view follows the craze
involving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze
an angle is a view or point of view

explanation.surface: A sceptic asks for a view on some navy-wide fad and dismisses it as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the view after the craze.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old-fashioned word for showy, useless frippery, and by extension silly fuss or rubbish.

clue.text: End with 'Keel Row' rearranged — crafty stuff

indicators.note: rearranged signals that the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the title of a Tyneside folk song

explanation.surface: A folk-song arrangement ends with The Keel Row, shuffled about by a crafty musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' works on END plus KEELROW. 'crafty' is used in its sense of to do with crafts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewing and embroidery are handicrafts, so the material and work of them is literally craft work.

clue.text: Minister, Father, recalled leaderless flock

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters are turned round
leaderless means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a herd is a flock or group of animals

explanation.surface: A clergyman, a father figure, remembers a congregation with no one leading it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like part of a list of clergy titles, but it is wordplay; only 'Minister' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain in the armed forces, a minister of religion serving troops.

clue.text: Drink? Small measure of spirits overturned by girl nursing soft drink

indicators.note: overturned, in a down clue, means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name
cola is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: A girl holding a soft drink knocks over someone's tot of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: This cocktail of rum, coconut and pineapple is a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: Fool snatching woman's cigar

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing hold of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coot, after the bird, is a silly old fool
her is the possessive for a woman's

explanation.surface: A fool grabs a woman's cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling someone a silly old coot is everyday British usage, from the bald-looking water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheroot is a cigar with both ends cut square.

clue.text: Pseudonym, say, fake, leading to incomplete cover

indicators.note: leading to means coming first, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: cod means fake or mock, as in a cod accent

indicators.note: incomplete means the last letter is removed

parts.note: enamel is a protective coating or cover

explanation.surface: A false name, a sham that leads to a cover story only half complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts ENAMEL to ENAME, and COD goes ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A code name is an assumed name, and a pseudonym is one example of such a disguised identity.

clue.text: Writer, racy, expressing hint of sadism in punishment

parts.note: a pen is something you write with

indicators.note: expressing means pressing out, so that letter is squeezed out of the word

parts.note: salty means racy or earthy, as in salty language

indicators.note: a hint of means just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A racy writer's work betrays a whiff of sadism in its punishments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hint of sadism' is S; 'expressing' presses it out of SALTY to leave ALTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A penalty is a punishment imposed for breaking a rule or law.

clue.text: Duke's supporter to take time

parts.note: D is an abbreviation for duke
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A duke's backer is told to take his time.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to dawdle or linger, using up time.

clue.text: Celestial bodies to colour unusual opening of diorama

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters are arranged in an odd new way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Instructions to paint the celestial bodies in a strange way at the start of a museum diorama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges TO COLOUR; the first letter of diorama, D, ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vast shell of icy objects thought to surround the solar system, home of long-period comets.

clue.text: Extent of French rapacity putting Germany off

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: putting off means removing, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: greed is rapacity, grasping desire
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A judgement on how far French greed went in putting off the Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting Germany off' removes the final D from GREED to leave GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Degree means extent or amount, as in 'to some degree'.

clue.text: That's a good idea after the laryngitis cure

definitions.meaning: a reply welcoming a proposal, roughly 'that's more like it'
literally what one might say to a patient whose lost voice has just come back

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: laryngitis takes the voice away, so once it is cured the patient can speak again.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom of approval, said when someone finally makes an attractive offer or suggestion.

clue.text: Nothing on telerecording for poet

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, means placed above the next piece

parts.note: O, the round zero, means nothing
a vid is a video, a recording from television

explanation.surface: A recording of a poet that turns out to show nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovid was the Roman poet of the Metamorphoses.

clue.text: Fabric originating in Indonesian knotting and tying

indicators.note: where each word originates is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cloth whose origins lie in Indonesian methods of knotting and tying threads.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the yarns are tied and dyed before weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikat is a woven cloth made with yarns resist-dyed before weaving, typical of Indonesia.

clue.text: Composer less curtailed about skill

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece goes around the other
curtailed means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: minus means less, as in five less two
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A composer whose output has been cut short, all about artistry.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's name is properly written with a ring over the U, ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohuslav Martinu was a twentieth-century Czech composer of symphonies and operas.

clue.text: English father returned, snatching daughter producing bureaucratic snarl-up?

indicators.note: snatching means grabbing, so one piece is taken inside the other
returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: pater is Latin, and old schoolboy slang, for father

explanation.surface: An English father comes home, grabs his daughter and leaves a bureaucratic mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses both English and father together, giving RETAPE before the daughter goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is excessive official procedure that delays things, named after ribbon once used to tie up documents.
